official_measurement_examples.name: 2025 private-supply scale
official_measurement_examples.fact: DWI 2025 reporting records 34,102 private water supplies and 818,213 people supplied in England, with 3,119 sources reported without a risk assessment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Five-year risk assessment cycle
official_measurement_examples.fact: DWI Regulation 6 guidance states local authorities must risk assess applicable private water supply systems at least every five years, subject to the detailed regulatory exceptions and review duties.

official_measurement_examples.name: Regulation 9 threshold
official_measurement_examples.fact: DWI guidance states Regulation 9 covers supplies of 10 cubic metres or more per day for domestic purposes and supplies used as part of public or commercial activity.

official_measurement_examples.name: Regulation 10 distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: DWI guidance distinguishes smaller non-commercial private supplies and single-dwelling supplies under Regulation 10 from Regulation 9 supplies.

official_measurement_examples.name: New-supply use gate
official_measurement_examples.fact: DWI Regulation 13 guidance states a new or reinstated private supply for domestic purposes should not be put into use until required risk assessment and monitoring steps have been completed.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2018 amendment currency
official_measurement_examples.fact: DWI legislation guidance records that the Private Water Supplies England Amendment Regulations 2018 came into force on 11 July 2018.

official_measurement_examples.name: 16 July 2026 report publication
official_measurement_examples.fact: DWI published its Drinking Water 2025 private water supplies annual reports on 16 July 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: Water quality versus capacity
official_measurement_examples.fact: DWI risk-assessment and monitoring duties address wholesomeness and public-health risk and do not by themselves establish future source yield or development capacity.
